# `extension-changed-wire`

x- extension the policy classifies as wire changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` |
| **Rule IDs** | `extension-changed-wire` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M6) |
| **Group** | Docs (annotations only) ([RULES.md section 10](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An `x-` extension that the policy's `extensions` section classifies as `wire` changed: one that changes what servers or gateways accept or send.

## Why this default

The extension affects behaviour on the wire, but api-diff can't tell how, so it might break clients.

## Example

From test case [`extension-changed-wire`](../../test/cases/extension-changed-wire/): The policy classifies x-rate-limit as wire: lowering it is extension-changed-wire (warn).

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
      get:
        operationId: listPets
-       x-rate-limit: 100
+       x-rate-limit: 10
        responses:
          '200':
```

Findings:

- `extension-changed-wire` · warn · GET /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  extension-changed-wire: warn
```

## How to fix

Check what the extension controls; keep the old value if clients depend on it.
